## make a simple regression model

```{r}
bears <- read.csv(file="BEARS.csv",header = TRUE)
#adjust factors to be factors
bears$SEX<- as.factor(bears$SEX)
bears$MONTH<- as.factor(bears$MONTH)
```

## Model LENGTH ~ NECK  this is an example 

```{r}
plot(LENGTH ~ NECK,data=bears,pch=19)
```  

As the neck circumference increases, so does the neck lenght.the plot is primarily linear.


```{r}
model.1 <- lm(LENGTH ~ NECK,data=bears)
summary.lm(model.1)
```

The adjust R-squared is 0.7476.
 
 
Compare all models that predict LENGTH other  thanNECK.  
Then order them from worst to best by its value of Adjusted-Rsquared (bigger is better), or by RSE (residual standard error) where smaller is better. 

## Model LENGTH ~ HEADLEN  

```{r}
plot(LENGTH ~ HEADLEN,data=bears,pch=19)
```


As the head length increases, so does the length of the bear. However, this box plot is not entirely linear. 


```{r}
model.2 <- lm(LENGTH ~ HEADLEN,data=bears)
summary.lm(model.2)
```

The adjusted R-squared is 0.8434, which is bigger than the previous models.  


## Model LENGTH ~ HeadWTH

```{r}
plot(LENGTH ~ HEADWTH,data=bears,pch=19)
```  


It shows that as head with increases so does length but almost at a slower rate. the plot is mainly linear with an upward trend. slight deviation.


```{r}
model.3 <- lm(LENGTH ~ HEADWTH,data=bears)
summary.lm(model.3)
```   



the Adjusted R-Squared is 0.5321  


## Model LENGTH ~ CHEST

```{r}
plot(LENGTH ~ CHEST,data=bears,pch=19)
```
  
similar to the two previous plots, As chest measurements increase, so does the overall length of bear.The plot is still somewhat linear, again fallowing an upward trend, with a bit of deviation.    


```{r}
model.4 <- lm(LENGTH ~ CHEST,data=bears)
summary.lm(model.4)
```  

The Adjusted R-squared is 0.7869, making it the second largest.  


## Model LENGTH ~ WEIGHT  

```{r}
plot(LENGTH ~ WEIGHT, data=bears,pch=19)
```  

As the weight of the bear increases, length also increase mainly at the beginning of the plot. this makes the beginning of the plot deviate a bit from the usual linear plot.


```{r}
model.5 <- lm(LENGTH ~ WEIGHT,data=bears)
summary.lm(model.5)
```  
The Adjusted R-Square is 0.7423. making it one of the lowest numbers.


## Final Rank  
#### In order from biggest to smallest adjusted R-squared values.

A) 0.8434
B) 0.7869
C) 0.7476
D) 0.7423
E) 0.5321
